description: REQ-012(c) and REQ-012's own Acceptance Criteria explicitly require that `checkSourceFunded`'s `requiredBaseUnits` argument, AS ACTUALLY PASSED BY THE DRIVER, be bit-identical to the same value routed to Skip's `amount_in` and BaseSigner's tx amount (behavioral-spec.md:238-244, 533-536) -- this is the FIND-003 (iteration-4) fix. But that same driver-level-identity discipline is never extended, in the normative EARS/Acceptance-Criteria text, to the OTHER two literal constants that were pinned this same iteration: `MIN_GAS_WEI` (REQ-003, behavioral-spec.md:194-244) and `TOLERANCE_BPS` (REQ-007, behavioral-spec.md:358-389). REQ-003's EARS clause states `minGasWei` 'is ALWAYS the literal constant MIN_GAS_WEI' (line 201) and REQ-007's EARS clause states `toleranceBps` 'is ALWAYS the literal constant TOLERANCE_BPS = 50' (line 364) -- both are normative claims about what value the constant equals, but neither REQ's Acceptance Criteria section requires a test to confirm the DRIVER's actual runtime argument to `checkSourceFunded`'s `minGasWei` parameter (resp. `verifySettlement`'s `toleranceBps` parameter) is that literal value, as opposed to merely asserting the pure function's comparison logic is correct when TEST CODE supplies that literal directly. Compare REQ-003's Acceptance Criteria bullet for `requiredBaseUnits` ('A test asserts the driver's ACTUAL runtime argument to checkSourceFunded's requiredBaseUnits parameter is bit-identical...', line 238) against the complete absence of an equivalent 'driver's ACTUAL runtime argument to checkSourceFunded's minGasWei parameter' clause anywhere in REQ-003, and the complete absence of an equivalent 'driver's ACTUAL runtime argument to verifySettlement's toleranceBps parameter' clause anywhere in REQ-007. For a money-path spec that itself states 'capUsd() and toBaseUnits() each passing their own isolated unit tests is explicitly NOT sufficient evidence that this requirement holds -- only the driver-level call-argument assertion is' (behavioral-spec.md:313-315) as the operating principle, applying that principle to only one of the three constants pinned this iteration (requiredBaseUnits) and not the other two (MIN_GAS_WEI, TOLERANCE_BPS) is an unreconciled, asymmetric gap in the normative text itself.

evidence.snippet: where `minGasWei` is ALWAYS the literal constant `MIN_GAS_WEI = 1_000_000_000_000_000n`... [REQ-003's Acceptance Criteria never requires a driver-level runtime-argument-identity test for minGasWei, unlike its own requiredBaseUnits bullet at line 238-244] ... The slippage tolerance is ALWAYS the literal constant `TOLERANCE_BPS = 50`... [REQ-007's Acceptance Criteria never requires a driver-level runtime-argument-identity test for toleranceBps]

fix: Add an Acceptance Criteria bullet to REQ-003 requiring a test that asserts the driver's ACTUAL runtime argument to checkSourceFunded's minGasWei parameter is bit-identical to MIN_GAS_WEI (inspected via spy call arguments, not the pure function's return value in isolation). Add a symmetric Acceptance Criteria bullet to REQ-007 requiring a test that asserts the driver's ACTUAL runtime argument to verifySettlement's toleranceBps parameter is bit-identical to TOLERANCE_BPS.
